description: What a CRM knows — people, organizations and deals as facts with the revision they were read at: title, company, owner, stage, amount, dates, source. Records enter deterministically through the records door (no model call); prose fields (notes) go to the ordinary extractor.

sources.title: Pushed records (webhook / automation)
sources.description: Record envelopes posted by a CRM outbound webhook or an automation (Make, n8n, Zapier, Albato, a script) to POST /v1/source-connections/<id>/records with a brain:write key — batches of { entityType, externalId, name, attributes, relations?, updatedAt? } plus the ids that are gone. No polling, no credential on the brain. config: { mapping? }.

sources.title: Pipedrive
sources.description: Deals, persons and organizations of a Pipedrive account, incrementally through updated_since + cursor (API v2), as a connected account or with an API token. config: { entities?, mapping?, apiDomain? }.

sources.title: HubSpot
sources.description: Deals, contacts and companies of a HubSpot portal, incrementally through the CRM Search API (last-modified windows + cursor; associations read per page), as a connected account or with a private-app access token. config: { entities?, mapping? }.

sources.title: Bitrix24
sources.description: Deals, leads, contacts and companies of a Bitrix24 portal through crm.item.list (filter[>updatedTime] + start), stages / sources / pipelines resolved to names, as a connected account (a local / Marketplace application) or with an inbound webhook URL as the credential. config: { entities?, mapping?, allowPrivate? }.

sources.title: Kommo / amoCRM
sources.description: Leads (deals), contacts and companies of a Kommo or amoCRM account through API v4 (filter[updated_at][from] + page), statuses / pipelines / users resolved to names, as a connected account or with a long-lived token of a private integration and the account URL. config: { baseUrl?, entities?, mapping? }.

sources.title: Salesforce
sources.description: Opportunities, contacts, accounts (and leads, cases) of a Salesforce org through SOQL over REST (LastModifiedDate > since, nextRecordsUrl; the deleted-ids feed closes deletions), Bulk API 2.0 for a large org's first walk, as a connected account or as an integration user (JWT bearer). config: { entities?, mapping?, instanceUrl?, loginUrl?, apiVersion?, bulk? }.

sources.title: Custom REST / OpenAPI
sources.description: Any CRM, ERP or ticketing backend with a JSON list API and no connector of its own: its endpoints described as config (list path, where the rows sit, paging style, updated-since parameter, id / name / updated-at fields, relations) — proposed by the mapping assistant from an OpenAPI document or a sample answer, verified by the preview. config: { baseUrl, authScheme?, endpoints, entities?, mapping? }.

predicates.description:
TYPE   subject is a person; value is their role at their organization
ADMIT  a CRM record or text names the person's title ("Head of Procurement")
VALUE  the title verbatim

TYPE   subject is a person, organization or deal; value is the CRM user responsible for it
ADMIT  the record names its owner / responsible user
VALUE  the owner's name verbatim

TYPE   subject is a person or deal; value is where it came from
ADMIT  the record names a source / channel ("Inbound web form", "Referral")
VALUE  the source verbatim

TYPE   subject is a person or organization; value is its lifecycle stage in the CRM
ADMIT  the record carries a lifecycle / status field ("lead", "customer", "churned")
VALUE  the stage verbatim

TYPE   subject is an organization; value is its industry
ADMIT  the record names the organization's industry / sector
VALUE  the industry verbatim

TYPE   subject is an organization; value is its website
ADMIT  the record carries a website / domain
VALUE  the URL or domain verbatim

TYPE   subject is a deal; value is the pipeline stage it is in
ADMIT  the record names the deal's current stage ("Negotiation", "Proposal sent")
VALUE  the stage label verbatim — the CRM's own name for it

TYPE   subject is a deal; value is open / won / lost (or the CRM's equivalent)
ADMIT  the record carries a status field
VALUE  the status verbatim

TYPE   subject is a deal; value is its monetary value
ADMIT  the record carries a value / amount
VALUE  the amount as the CRM states it ("40000")

TYPE   subject is a deal; value is the currency of its amount
ADMIT  the record names a currency code
VALUE  the code verbatim ("EUR")

TYPE   subject is a deal; value is the pipeline it belongs to
ADMIT  the record names its pipeline
VALUE  the pipeline name verbatim

TYPE   subject is a deal; value is the CRM's win probability
ADMIT  the record carries a probability
VALUE  the number as stated ("60")

TYPE   subject is a deal; value is the expected close date
ADMIT  the record carries an expected / planned close date
VALUE  the date as stated

TYPE   subject is a deal; value is when it was won
ADMIT  the record carries a won time
VALUE  the timestamp as stated

TYPE   subject is a deal; value is when it was lost
ADMIT  the record carries a lost time
VALUE  the timestamp as stated

TYPE   subject is a deal; value is why it was lost
ADMIT  the record carries a lost reason
VALUE  the reason verbatim

TYPE   subject is a deal; value is the agreed next activity
ADMIT  the record or text names the next step ("send revised proposal by Friday")
VALUE  the step verbatim

TYPE   subject is a person, organization or deal; value is when it was last touched
ADMIT  the record carries a last-activity time
VALUE  the timestamp as stated

TYPE   subject is any record; value is a tag / label the CRM applies
ADMIT  the record carries labels or tags
VALUE  one label per fact (multi-valued)

extractionProfile.guidance:
CRM inputs are RECORDS (contacts, organizations, deals) — their structured
fields arrive as facts by themselves; this profile is for the PROSE they
carry: notes, call summaries, next steps. Treat the record's subject (the
person, organization or deal named in the title) as the SUBJECT entity.
Prefer crm_memory__next_step for agreed actions, crm_memory__lost_reason
for why a deal was lost, crm_memory__deal_stage only when a stage is named
verbatim. Copy values VERBATIM — "send revised proposal by Friday", not a
paraphrase.

fewShot.text: Call with Acme Robotics: they asked for a revised proposal by Friday; budget owner is Grace Hopper.
fewShot.note: deal/organization 'Acme Robotics' → crm_memory__next_step='revised proposal by Friday'; person 'Grace Hopper' → crm_memory__owner is NOT this (owner = the CRM user), but a relation to Acme.

fewShot.text: Lost to a cheaper competitor after the pilot; the deal moved to Lost.
fewShot.note: → crm_memory__lost_reason='cheaper competitor after the pilot', crm_memory__deal_stage='Lost'.
